technique.summary: Exploit inconsistencies between URL parsers (the one used for validation vs. the one used for fetching) to bypass SSRF protections. Different libraries parse authority, host, port, and path components differently.
steps: Identify the SSRF protection mechanism (allowlist, blocklist, regex)
Test various URL authority formats: user@host, host\@attacker, host#fragment
Test backslash vs forward slash handling: http://attacker\@target
Test Unicode normalization: fullwidth characters, homoglyphs
Test scheme handling: gopher://, dict://, file:///
Confirm which parser handles validation vs. actual request

payloads.notes: Authority confusion — validator sees target.com, fetcher resolves evil.com
Unicode fullwidth characters — may normalize to evil.com

bypassTechniques: Use different URL schemes (gopher, dict, file) if supported
Chain with open redirect on allowed domain
Null byte injection in URL: http://allowed.com%00.evil.com
